answer: Proof-of-latency fingerprinting: each agent must answer a random cipher puzzle from several geographically spread verifiers within tight timing windows, so one server cannot pose as many distinct agents. Like counting yarrow stalks for a reading, the verifier tallies round-trip times; clones share a network path and their profiles collapse together. An attacker must rent separate machines in separate regions per identity, which costs far more than saffron by weight.
